use_case: Student-progress risk scoring (AI progress insights module): flags students at risk of falling behind and recommends sessions per week
vendor_or_model: Tutoring platform vendor (machine learning feature inside the vendor SaaS; vendor model)
data_categories: Practice exercise accuracy and time on task; attendance; session counts; grade level; platform assessment scores; district assessment scores for program students (children's personal information; district education records)
human_in_the_loop: Tutor judgment decides every placement with a recorded reason; no reduction or removal of services based on a flag; no use in sales messages
applicable_laws: COPPA Rule 16 CFR 312.4(b), 312.5(a)(1)-(2), 312.8(c), 312.10; FERPA conditions through the district contract (34 CFR 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B), 99.33(a)(2)); Fla. Stat. 501.171; FTC Act Section 5 (claims to parents)
status: Approved with conditions; turned off 2026-08-28 until the conditions are met (private-pay students only on restart; district students need district approval)

use_case: Public generative AI chatbots used by tutors to draft practice worksheets and lesson ideas
data_categories: None allowed; risk of student work or names being pasted
risk_tier: Low (no student data); High if student data is entered
applicable_laws: COPPA Rule 312.5(a)(2) and FERPA redisclosure limits (99.33(a)) if student information were entered
status: Allowed for generic content only; prohibited for Restricted data (POL-04 4.6; POL-02 C.2)

use_case: Generative AI homework helper chatbot offered by the tutoring platform for students to use between sessions
vendor_or_model: Tutoring platform vendor (generative language model feature)
data_categories: Would process children's questions, work, and possibly voice (children's personal information)
risk_tier: Medium (interacts directly with children); reassess before any use
human_in_the_loop: Not designed; would need tutor oversight of conversations
applicable_laws: COPPA Rule (notice, consent, and separate consent for any AI training use, 312.5(a)(2)); FTC Act Section 5
status: Not enabled; turning it on requires its own assessment and Owner approval
